Before we build the panel, one thing needs your call: **what should the panel be made of, and where should it live on the server?**

Why it matters: the panel has to do the four jobs you named — edit the Palworld server's settings, take a movie or TV show name and send it to the downloader, give you quick access to the AI you're testing, and let you reach scaffold-engine. All four mean the panel has to talk to other things on the server. The choice below decides how easy that is to build and keep working.

Here are the options, in plain words:

**Option 1 — A small custom web page in its own container (Python).**
The panel is a little program we write, running in its own isolated box on the server (a container — think of it as a mini-computer that only runs this one thing). You open it in your browser like any web page. Python is the language it's written in — the same family of tools your AI box already uses, so there's less new stuff to learn and maintain. Trade-off: it takes a bit of time to build, and the look is simple rather than fancy.

**Option 2 — A small custom web page in its own container (Node.js + a modern frontend).**
Same idea — a custom panel in its own container — but built with a different set of tools that make the page look and feel more polished, with smoother buttons and screens. Trade-off: more moving parts to keep updated over time, and a second set of tools to maintain alongside the AI stack.

**Option 3 — A ready-made dashboard (like Homarr or Dashy) with links and buttons.**
Instead of writing a custom panel, we install an existing dashboard program and arrange it to show the things you want. Fastest to get something on screen. Trade-off: it's mostly links and shortcuts — typing a movie name to download and editing the Palworld settings directly would need extra workarounds or separate small tools anyway, so the "one stop" feel is weaker.

**Where it runs in all three cases:** on the Proxmox server itself, in its own container, reachable from your home network. Nothing is exposed to the outside unless we later decide to — and that's a separate question we haven't answered yet.

Which of these sounds right — or would you rather I narrow it down by asking what you most want to be able to do first?
